steps.intent: France’s priority is to prevent the expiration of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism and preserve the Council’s ability to investigate and attribute chemical weapons attacks in Syria. To avoid a Russian veto, the draft is limited to a short technical rollover while retaining clear language on accountability and cooperation. The main difficulty will be Russian resistance to any renewed mandate and attempts to weaken references to responsibility or to link the extension to broader political conditions.
steps.text:
The Security Council,
Recalling its resolutions 2118 (2013), 2209 (2015), 2235 (2015), 2319 (2016) and 2332 (2016), and the relevant decisions of the OPCW Executive Council,
Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic,
Recalling the establishment of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism by resolution 2235 (2015) and the extension of its mandate by resolution 2319 (2016) until 17 November 2017,
Taking note of the report of the Joint Investigative Mechanism of 26 October 2017 and expressing grave concern at its findings and at continuing reports of chemical weapons use in the Syrian Arab Republic,
Reaffirming that the use of chemical weapons constitutes a serious violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security, and that those responsible for any such use must be held accountable,
Stressing the need for the Joint Investigative Mechanism to continue its work in an impartial, objective and independent manner, and for all parties to cooperate fully with it, including by providing unhindered and safe access,
Determining that the situation in the Syrian Arab Republic continues to constitute a threat to international peace and security,
Acting under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations,
1. Decides to extend the mandate of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism, as set out in resolution 2235 (2015) and extended by resolution 2319 (2016), for a period of 30 days, until 18 December 2017;
2. Requests the Joint Investigative Mechanism to continue to report to the Security Council, as appropriate, on the implementation of its mandate;
3. Calls upon all parties in the Syrian Arab Republic and all other relevant parties to cooperate fully with the Joint Investigative Mechanism and the OPCW, and to ensure unhindered and safe access to all relevant sites, persons and information;
4. Reaffirms that those responsible for the use of chemical weapons must be held accountable, and urges all Member States to cooperate fully with the Joint Investigative Mechanism and the OPCW in this regard;
5. Decides to remain seized of the matter.

Bolivia (Plurinational State of).change: Replace 'expressing grave concern at its findings and at continuing reports of chemical weapons use' with 'taking note of the report and stressing that its findings must be based on credible, verifiable evidence, without politicization or prejudgment'.

Replace 'for a period of 30 days, until 18 December 2017' with 'for a period of six months, until 17 May 2018, subject to the Joint Investigative Mechanism revising its methodology and fully respecting the sovereignty of the Syrian Arab Republic'.

Add: 'Requests the Joint Investigative Mechanism to report to the Council on its methodology and evidentiary basis and to address concerns raised by Member States before any further attribution of responsibility.'

Add: 'Reaffirms that the work of the Joint Investigative Mechanism must not be used to undermine the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of the Syrian Arab Republic or to justify unilateral action.'

China.change: Replace “Taking note of the report of the Joint Investigative Mechanism of 26 October 2017 and expressing grave concern at its findings and at continuing reports of chemical weapons use in the Syrian Arab Republic,” with “Taking note of the report of the Joint Investigative Mechanism of 26 October 2017 and noting the continuing reports of chemical weapons use in the Syrian Arab Republic, while stressing that the Mechanism’s conclusions require further impartial and objective examination and should not prejudge the outcome of any comprehensive review,”

Replace “Decides to extend the mandate of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism, as set out in resolution 2235 (2015) and extended by resolution 2319 (2016), for a period of 30 days, until 18 December 2017;” with “Decides to extend the mandate of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism, as set out in resolution 2235 (2015) and extended by resolution 2319 (2016), for a technical period of 30 days, until 18 December 2017, without prejudice to a comprehensive review of its mandate and without constituting a precedent for further extension;”

Add: “Decides to review the mandate and working methods of the Joint Investigative Mechanism in light of its forthcoming report and on the basis of consensus before any further extension is considered;”
Add: “Reaffirming the importance of the Security Council maintaining unity and consensus on the question of chemical weapons in Syria and avoiding politicization;”

Russian Federation.change: Delete 'and expressing grave concern at its findings' and replace 'Taking note of the report of the Joint Investigative Mechanism of 26 October 2017' with 'Taking note of the report of the Joint Investigative Mechanism of 26 October 2017, while noting that its conclusions require further review and must not prejudge the work of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission'.
Replace 'for a period of 30 days, until 18 December 2017' with 'for a period of six months, until 17 May 2018'.

Add after OP1: 'Requests the Secretary-General, in coordination with the Director-General of the OPCW, to submit within 30 days proposals for the reconfiguration of the Joint Investigative Mechanism's structure and methodology, and decides that the Mechanism shall not attribute responsibility for any incident until the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission has completed its investigation of that incident and its report has been considered by the Security Council.'
Add 'and stresses that cooperation must be provided without politicization or preconditions by all parties, including the Syrian Government and all other relevant parties'.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia cannot support the current text, which endorses the JIM's October findings without addressing serious concerns about methodology and politicization. We need neutral language on the report, a longer extension tied to a revised methodology, and clear guarantees that the mechanism respects Syria's sovereignty and is not used for political purposes.
messages.China: China firmly opposes the use of chemical weapons under any circumstances and supports an impartial, objective and independent investigation by the Joint Investigative Mechanism. However, the current text is not based on consensus and appears to prejudge the Mechanism’s findings; China cannot support it as drafted. We request that the extension be clearly described as a technical rollover pending a comprehensive review of the mandate, and that the language on the 26 October report be balanced so as not to prejudge the outcome. Without such changes, China will abstain.
messages.Egypt: Egypt supports the draft as it stands. The 30-day extension is a necessary technical rollover to prevent a gap in the JIM's work, and we urge all Council members to support it. We call on all parties in Syria to cooperate fully with the JIM and the OPCW.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia supports the draft as a pragmatic, time-bound extension that preserves the institutional continuity of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism and avoids a gap while its final report is awaited. We believe Council unity is essential on chemical-weapons accountability, and we call on all parties to cooperate fully with the Mechanism and the OPCW. We therefore support the text as circulated.
messages.Italy: Italy is proud to co-sponsor this draft, which preserves the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism and its vital work on accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria. We strongly support the 30-day extension as a pragmatic step to prevent a gap in the Mechanism's mandate and urge all Council members to vote in favour. While Italy would have preferred a longer renewal for the sake of continuity and predictability, we will not propose amendments at this stage and hope the Council can soon return to the question of a further extension.
messages.Japan: Japan fully supports the draft and is pleased to co-sponsor it. The JIM must be able to continue its work without interruption, and this 30-day extension is the minimum necessary to preserve accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria. We urge all Council members to support the text as it stands and call on all parties to cooperate fully with the JIM and the OPCW.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan supports this draft as a necessary technical rollover that prevents a gap in the JIM’s work and allows the Council to consider the 26 October report. We appreciate the balanced language on impartiality, full cooperation by all parties, and accountability. We urge all members to preserve Council unity so that the Mechanism can continue without further interruption.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support this draft as it stands. The 30-day extension is politically motivated, and the reference to the 26 October report prejudges an unfinished process. We insist on removing that prejudicial language and adding a clear requirement for the JIM to coordinate with the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and refrain from attribution until its work is complete. If these red lines are not addressed, we will have no choice but to veto.
messages.Senegal: Senegal supports the draft as a necessary technical extension to prevent a gap in the JIM’s work and to preserve accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria. While we would have preferred a longer renewal, we accept the 30-day extension as a bridge and urge all Council members to support it. All parties must cooperate fully with the JIM and OPCW, and the Mechanism must continue its impartial, objective and independent work.
messages.Sweden: Sweden fully supports this draft as a co-sponsor. A 30-day extension is the minimum necessary to prevent a gap in the JIM’s work and to preserve the possibility of accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria. We urge all Council members to adopt the text without delay and will not press amendments at this stage.
messages.Ukraine: Ukraine, as a co-sponsor, supports the draft as it stands and urges the Council to adopt it without delay. The JIM must be allowed to continue its impartial and independent work, and the Council cannot permit another failure on accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria. We call on all members to vote in favour and on all parties to cooperate fully, including by ensuring unhindered and safe access.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the draft as co-sponsored. A 30-day extension is the minimum necessary to keep the Joint Investigative Mechanism operational and to preserve the Council’s ability to hold chemical-weapons users accountable. We see no need for changes at this stage and call on all Council members, particularly Russia, not to block this technical extension.
messages.United States of America: The United States co-sponsors this draft and supports it as written. The Joint Investigative Mechanism must be extended immediately to avoid any gap in its work, and we view this 30-day extension as a necessary stopgap. We urge all Council members to join us in adopting the text without delay.
messages.Uruguay: Uruguay supports this draft as a necessary technical rollover to prevent a gap in the JIM’s work and to protect its staff and institutional memory. We urge all Council members to adopt it without delay. We hope the Council will return to a longer and more predictable renewal as soon as possible.

replies.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): partially accepted: added credible-evidence language and methodology reporting; rejected six-month precondition and sovereignty conditions.
replies.China: partially accepted: accepted technical rollover, review clause, and unity language; retained core grave concern.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: added OP3 language on the Syrian Government and preconditions; rejected red lines on the report, six-month extension, and attribution restrictions.

steps.summary: The revised text makes limited, non-substantive accommodations to China and Bolivia while preserving the JIM’s independent attribution mandate and retaining the 30-day technical extension. France cannot accept Russian red lines that would condition or prohibit attribution, so the draft is expected to be vetoed by Russia despite broad support.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia appreciates the addition of credible-evidence and methodology language, but the text still prejudges the JIM’s findings by expressing grave concern before a full review of its methodology. We cannot support a 30-day extension that lacks safeguards for Syrian sovereignty and against politicization. Unless PP4 is corrected and the sovereignty safeguard is included, Bolivia will not support the draft.
messages.China: China welcomes the technical rollover, the review clause and the language on Council unity, which address our core concern against an open-ended extension. However, we cannot accept language that expresses grave concern at the Mechanism’s findings before the comprehensive review and without a consensus basis for any further extension. If PP3 and OP5 are not adjusted, China will abstain on the current text.
messages.Egypt: Egypt supports the 30-day technical extension of the JIM as a compromise that keeps the accountability mechanism alive. We stress that the Mechanism’s conclusions must remain impartial and evidence-based and that all parties, including the Syrian Government, must cooperate fully. We hope this period allows the Council to reach consensus on a comprehensive review and future extension.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia supports the draft as a balanced compromise that preserves the Joint Investigative Mechanism’s institutional continuity for a technical period while reaffirming impartiality, accountability and Council unity. We welcome the emphasis on credible, verifiable evidence and the call on all parties to cooperate fully. Ethiopia will vote in favour and urges all members to maintain consensus on this matter.
messages.Italy: Italy supports the draft as co-sponsored. The 30-day technical extension is the minimum necessary to prevent a dangerous gap in the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism’s work, and Italy urges all Council members to preserve unity and allow the Mechanism to continue its impartial, objective and independent investigation. We call on all parties in Syria to cooperate fully and without preconditions, including by ensuring unhindered and safe access, and we remain ready to consider further extension in light of the Mechanism’s forthcoming report.
messages.Japan: Japan supports the current revised text and thanks the penholder for the compromise. Extending the JIM for 30 days is essential to avoid a gap and preserve the Mechanism’s ability to continue its impartial work. Japan urges all Council members to support the draft so that accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria can be pursued without interruption.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan supports the revised text as a balanced, time-limited technical extension that preserves the Joint Investigative Mechanism while allowing the Council to assess its forthcoming report. We urge all members to maintain Council unity and avoid politicization of this issue. We call on all parties in Syria to cooperate fully with the JIM and the OPCW, including by ensuring unhindered and safe access.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation notes the addition in OP3, but the current text still endorses the JIM report's findings before a proper review and maintains an artificial 30-day deadline. Unless the red lines on PP4, OP1 and the new OP on methodology and attribution are reflected, we will not be in a position to support the draft.
messages.Senegal: Senegal supports the revised draft as a pragmatic technical extension of the Joint Investigative Mechanism for 30 days, which is necessary to preserve the Mechanism and Council unity pending its forthcoming report. We urge all parties, including the Syrian Government, to cooperate fully and without preconditions, and we reiterate that those responsible for the use of chemical weapons must be held accountable. We look forward to the report and to the Council considering the future of the mandate on the basis of the JIM's independent and impartial work.
messages.Sweden: Sweden supports the revised draft as a necessary technical extension of the JIM, which must be allowed to continue its impartial and objective work. The 30-day extension is a compromise that preserves the Mechanism while the Council considers next steps; we urge all members to unite behind it and reject any further delay. There must be no impunity for chemical weapons use in Syria, and all parties must cooperate fully with the JIM and OPCW.
messages.Ukraine: Ukraine supports the revised draft as a co-sponsor. We see the 30-day technical extension as a necessary stopgap to preserve the Joint Investigative Mechanism's work and avoid impunity. We urge all Council members to support adoption and all parties in Syria to cooperate fully and without preconditions with the Mechanism and OPCW.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the draft as a pragmatic compromise that prevents a gap in the Joint Investigative Mechanism’s vital work. We urge all Council members to adopt it without delay and call on all parties, especially the Syrian regime, to cooperate fully with the Mechanism and the OPCW. We will continue to press for a full renewal and for accountability for all chemical weapons use in Syria.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the revised draft as circulated. It preserves the Joint Investigative Mechanism for a technical 30-day period so its impartial work can continue, and it keeps the Council focused on accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria. We urge all members to join us in supporting the text without further changes.
messages.Uruguay: Uruguay supports the revised draft as a necessary technical rollover to prevent a gap in the Joint Investigative Mechanism's work. We would have preferred a longer extension, but with the mandate expiring tomorrow, the Council should not delay adoption. We urge all members to vote in favour and to return to a comprehensive renewal before 18 December, including measures to retain JIM staff.

reasons.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia’s stated red line on PP4 and its other amendments were rejected, and its prior position was opposition. To act consistently with its sovereignty-focused, anti-politicization stance and the negotiation record, Bolivia votes no.
reasons.China: China sought softer language on the JIM report and a consensus basis for further extension; the partial acceptance was insufficient. An abstention avoids a veto while signaling concerns and preserving support for the JIM’s technical work.
reasons.Egypt: Egypt signalled support in the last negotiation round and has consistently voted to extend the JIM to preserve chemical-weapons accountability. A yes vote is consistent with its public posture on credible, non-politicized investigations.
reasons.Ethiopia: Ethiopia has consistently supported renewing the JIM, including voting for the October renewal draft, and its stated priority is accountability through an impartial mechanism with full Council unity. A 30-day technical extension fits that position and is likely to be supported before the Russian veto.
reasons.France: France is a co-sponsor and consistent supporter of the OPCW-UN JIM and accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria, so it votes in favour of the 30-day technical extension.
reasons.Italy: Italy co-sponsored the draft and has consistently supported renewing the OPCW-UN JIM to uphold chemical weapons accountability and Council unity. The 30-day technical extension aligns with its stated position and is preferable to allowing the mandate to expire.
reasons.Japan: Japan has consistently supported the JIM’s mandate and accountability for chemical weapons use, and it is a co-sponsor of this draft; a technical 30-day extension matches its stated priority of ensuring continuity while preserving Council unity.
reasons.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan has consistently supported preserving the JIM’s work and Council unity, and the 30-day technical extension fits its stated desire to assess the report before any comprehensive review. It therefore votes yes and explains its support before the vote.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia’s stated red lines on the JIM extension were rejected, and the draft preserves the 30-day extension and attribution framework it had opposed. Moscow would therefore vote against to maintain its established position and avoid endorsing a politicized mandate.
reasons.Senegal: Senegal has consistently voted for renewing the JIM and strongly condemns chemical weapons use, so it supports this 30-day technical extension. A pre-vote explanation aligns with its earlier statements appealing for Council unity and accountability.
reasons.Sweden: Sweden co-sponsored the draft and has consistently supported renewing the JIM to ensure accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria. A 30-day technical extension is consistent with Sweden’s stated position and therefore merits a yes vote.
reasons.Ukraine: Ukraine co-sponsored the draft and has consistently supported the JIM and accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria, so it votes in favour. A pre-vote statement reinforces that position and urges Council unity.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK co-sponsored the draft and consistently supports the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism; voting yes preserves the JIM and advances accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria.
reasons.United States of America: The United States has consistently supported renewing the JIM so it can continue investigating chemical weapons use in Syria. A 30-day extension is consistent with Washington’s goal of preventing the mandate from lapsing while seeking a longer-term renewal.
reasons.Uruguay: Uruguay has consistently supported JIM renewals and voted for the 24 October draft, emphasizing continuity, staff retention, and accountability; the 30-day technical extension aligns with that record and last-round support.

before.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia (Plurinational State of) unequivocally condemns the use of chemical weapons and supports the goal of accountability. However, my delegation cannot support this draft. It retains language that risks prejudging the findings of the Joint Investigative Mechanism and does not sufficiently guarantee that its conclusions are based on credible, verifiable and impartial evidence. The proposed 30-day extension is presented as technical, but it preserves a mechanism whose work has been deeply politicized and contested. Bolivia requested balanced amendments, including a longer renewal subject to methodological revision and full respect for the sovereignty of the Syrian Arab Republic, as well as an explicit affirmation that the Mechanism’s work must not be used to justify unilateral action or to undermine Syria’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence. Those requests were rejected. We therefore vote against this draft.
before.China: Mr. President, China opposes the use of chemical weapons under any circumstances and has consistently supported the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism in carrying out its mandate in an impartial, objective and independent manner. We support the continuation of the Mechanism’s work, but its mandate and working methods should be comprehensively reviewed, and any further extension should be considered on the basis of broad consultation and consensus within the Council. The draft before us contains some positive elements, including a technical extension and reference to a comprehensive review, but it retains language that prejudges the Mechanism’s findings and does not reflect the consensus basis that China has sought. China will therefore abstain on this draft resolution. We hope all parties will cooperate fully with the Mechanism and that the Council will handle this matter in a manner that preserves its unity and avoids politicization.
before.Egypt: Egypt will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We have consistently supported the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism and the principle that those responsible for the use of chemical weapons in Syria must be held accountable. The extension of the Mechanism’s mandate, even for a technical period of 30 days, is necessary to preserve its ability to complete its work. At the same time, Egypt stresses that the Mechanism must preserve its impartiality and objectivity, base its conclusions on credible and verifiable evidence, and that all parties, including the Syrian Government, must cooperate fully with it. This technical extension must not be used to politicize the issue or to prejudge the comprehensive review of the Mechanism’s mandate. Egypt will continue to support accountability, Council unity and full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity.
before.Ethiopia: Ethiopia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We have consistently held that the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism remains indispensable for establishing responsibility for chemical-weapons use in Syria and for deterring further use. We support this technical extension so that the Council can preserve institutional continuity and consider the Mechanism’s mandate in a calm and evidence-based manner. At the same time, we stress that the Mechanism’s conclusions must be impartial, objective and grounded in credible and verifiable evidence, and we call on all parties to cooperate fully with it. It remains our hope that the Council can restore unity on this critical issue and avoid politicization, because division here only weakens accountability and the prospects for peace.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The use of chemical weapons in Syria is a serious violation of international law and cannot go unpunished. The Joint Investigative Mechanism must be able to continue its impartial and independent work, including its examination of the grave findings in its report of 26 October. This text proposes a limited technical extension of 30 days, without prejudging the comprehensive review of the Mechanism’s mandate. It is balanced and does not seek to politicize the question. We call on all members of the Council to assume their responsibilities, to preserve Council unity and to allow the Mechanism to finish its work. Those responsible for chemical-weapons attacks must be held accountable, and France will continue to defend that principle.
before.Italy: Italy takes the floor in support of the draft resolution and will vote in favour. We are a co-sponsor because the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism must be allowed to continue its impartial and objective work to ensure accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria. The extension before us preserves the continuity of the Mechanism for a technical period and allows the Council time to consider its mandate and working methods in a comprehensive manner. We call on all parties in Syria to cooperate fully and without preconditions, and we urge the Council to preserve unity on this crucial non-proliferation issue. Allowing the Mechanism to lapse would weaken accountability and undermine the credibility of the international norm against chemical weapons.
before.Japan: Japan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism’s work is not complete, and its continued impartial and professional investigation is essential to ensuring accountability for the use of chemical weapons in Syria. A 30-day technical extension is a reasonable step to allow the Council to keep the Mechanism’s work going while it considers the mandate further. Japan urges all parties, including the Syrian Government, to cooperate fully and without preconditions with the Mechanism and the OPCW, and we stress that the Council must maintain unity and avoid politicization on this grave issue.
before.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan has consistently opposed the use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere, and supports the continuation of the OPCW–UN Joint Investigative Mechanism as an indispensable impartial and technical mechanism. With its mandate due to expire tomorrow, we believe there is no room for delay. We therefore support this 30-day technical extension, which is without prejudice to a comprehensive review and does not constitute a precedent, so that the Council can assess the Mechanism’s forthcoming report and consider the way forward in a calm, objective and united manner. We call on all parties in Syria, including the Syrian Government, to cooperate fully with the Mechanism and the OPCW and to ensure safe and unhindered access. It remains essential that the Security Council preserve its unity and avoid politicization. Kazakhstan will vote in favour.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation cannot support this draft. It has been prepared without genuine compromise and despite the red lines we set out, including the artificial 30-day extension and the retention of language that prejudges the Mechanism’s conclusions. We have consistently said that the Joint Investigative Mechanism must remain impartial, objective and fact-based, not be used as a tool of political pressure. The authors rejected our amendments, including our proposal for a six-month technical extension and the requirement that the Mechanism not attribute responsibility before the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission has completed its work and its report has been considered by the Council. This text therefore continues the politicization of the chemical weapons file and creates unacceptable conditions. The Russian Federation will vote against this draft resolution.
before.Senegal: Senegal will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We have consistently supported the work of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism because nothing can justify the use of chemical weapons. We regret that the Council is considering only a short technical extension, but we believe it is essential to preserve the Mechanism’s capacity to continue its impartial, independent and objective work and to avoid a vacuum in accountability. We call on all parties to cooperate fully with the Mechanism and urge the Council to maintain unity before considering any further extension.
before.Sweden: Sweden will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We co-sponsored it because the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism must be able to continue its essential work, and because the Security Council must not allow impunity for the use of chemical weapons in Syria. This is a technical extension, but it is necessary to preserve the Mechanism and to allow the Council to consider its mandate and working methods in a comprehensive manner. We urge all members to unite behind the JIM and behind accountability for chemical weapons use.
before.Ukraine: Ukraine co-sponsored this draft resolution and will vote in favour. The use of chemical weapons in Syria is a grave violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security, and the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism must be allowed to continue its independent and objective work. This technical extension is necessary to preserve the Mechanism while its mandate and working methods are reviewed. We call on all Council members to support accountability and on all parties in Syria, including the Syrian Government, to cooperate fully and without preconditions with the Mechanism and the OPCW.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr President, the United Kingdom will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The Joint Investigative Mechanism must be allowed to continue its work to identify those responsible for chemical weapons attacks in Syria, and its mandate should not be allowed to lapse while the Council considers the way forward. The use of chemical weapons is a grave violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. A short technical extension is not the outcome we would have wished for, but it is a necessary and pragmatic step to preserve the Mechanism’s capability and to avoid an operational gap. We call on all members of this Council to unite in support of accountability and to ensure that the Mechanism can complete its mandate in an impartial, objective and independent manner.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States strongly supports renewing the mandate of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism. The JIM’s impartial, expert work is essential to accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria, and we cannot allow its mandate to lapse. We support this 30-day technical extension to preserve the Mechanism while the Council considers its future. We call on all parties, including the Syrian regime, to cooperate fully and without conditions. We urge all members to vote in favour.
before.Uruguay: Uruguay will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism so that it can continue its work without interruption. As we stated on 24 October, the men and women of the JIM need certainty about their contracts and their future; a technical extension avoids an institutional gap and preserves the Mechanism’s capacity and expertise. Uruguay stresses that the use of chemical weapons is a serious violation of international law and that accountability must be upheld. We call on all parties, including the Syrian Government, to cooperate fully and without preconditions with the JIM and the OPCW, and we urge the Council to maintain unity and avoid politicization in addressing these serious issues.

after.Ethiopia:
Ethiopia regrets that the Council has not been able to adopt the draft resolution extending the mandate of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism. We voted in favour because the Mechanism remains indispensable for establishing responsibility for the use of chemical weapons in Syria and for deterring further use. Its work is not complete, and a technical extension would have preserved institutional continuity while allowing the Council to consider its mandate in a calm and evidence-based manner.

We continue to stress that the Mechanism’s conclusions must be impartial, objective and grounded in credible and verifiable evidence, and we call on all parties, including the Syrian Government, to cooperate fully with it. The use of chemical weapons cannot be tolerated, and accountability must be upheld without politicization. We hope that all members will continue efforts to restore the Council’s unity and to reach the necessary compromise on this critical issue.
after.France:
Thank you, Mr. President.

France voted in favour of this draft resolution and deeply regrets that it has not been adopted. The text was modest, balanced and technical: it sought only a 30-day extension of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism, without prejudice to the comprehensive review of its mandate, in order to avoid an operational gap and allow the Mechanism to continue its impartial and independent work, including on the grave findings of its report of 26 October.

The Russian Federation’s veto leaves the Council without the only international mechanism mandated to attribute responsibility for chemical weapons attacks in Syria. That is a grave abdication of our collective responsibility. It weakens accountability at the very moment when the use of chemical weapons must be rejected unequivocally. France recalls that the use of chemical weapons constitutes a serious violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. Those responsible must not enjoy impunity.

France will not accept the erosion of the chemical weapons taboo. We will continue to support the OPCW and to work with all partners who remain committed to accountability, to preserving evidence, and to ensuring that the Security Council can discharge its responsibilities. The veto must not become a licence for the use of chemical weapons.
after.Italy: Italy regrets that the Security Council has been unable to adopt this draft resolution, which we co-sponsored, owing to the negative vote of a permanent member. The OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism is not a political instrument; it is an essential technical mechanism charged with establishing responsibility for the use of chemical weapons in Syria. Its mandate expires tomorrow, and allowing it to lapse would create a dangerous vacuum in accountability and weaken the credibility of the international norm against chemical weapons. Italy remains firmly convinced that those responsible for chemical weapons use must be held accountable, and that the Mechanism must be able to continue its impartial, objective and independent work. We call on all parties in Syria to cooperate fully and without preconditions with the JIM and the OPCW. We also urge the Council to overcome its divisions and to find, without delay, a way to preserve the Mechanism’s continuity and to consider its mandate and working methods in a comprehensive manner. Accountability cannot be allowed to become a casualty of political disagreement.
after.Japan: Japan voted in favour of the draft resolution. We deeply regret that it was not adopted. The OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism’s work is not complete, and its continued impartial, objective and professional investigation is essential to ensuring accountability for the use of chemical weapons in Syria. The 30-day technical extension was a reasonable and pragmatic step to preserve the Mechanism’s continuity while the Council considers its mandate further, and it did not prejudge that review. Japan has full confidence in the Mechanism’s expertise and independence. We urge all parties in Syria, including the Syrian Government, to cooperate fully and without preconditions with the Joint Investigative Mechanism and the OPCW. The Security Council must not allow division to weaken the international norm against chemical weapons. Japan will continue to support efforts to ensure accountability and to restore Council unity on this grave issue.
after.Kazakhstan: Mr. President, Kazakhstan regrets that the Security Council has not been able to adopt this draft resolution. We voted in favour because the mandate of the OPCW–UN Joint Investigative Mechanism expires tomorrow, and an operational gap would seriously undermine its impartial, technical and objective work. We respect the positions of all Council members, including the Russian Federation, but we believe the fight against impunity for chemical weapons use must not weaken. We call on all members to engage in urgent consultations to preserve the Mechanism’s work and to consider its mandate and working methods in a comprehensive, calm and non-politicized manner. We also call on all parties in Syria, including the Syrian Government, to cooperate fully and without preconditions with the JIM and the OPCW. Kazakhstan remains committed to Council unity and to a political settlement of the Syrian crisis through the Astana and Geneva processes.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted against this draft resolution, and we want to explain our position clearly. We are not indifferent to the use of chemical weapons. Russia has consistently and unequivocally opposed the use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere, and we support the principle that those responsible must be held accountable. That is not the issue before the Council.

The issue is that this draft was not a technical, neutral text. It was prepared without genuine consultation and without taking into account the concerns of a significant part of the Council. The proposed 30-day extension was artificial. Its purpose was not to allow calm and comprehensive consideration of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism, but to create time pressure, to preserve a mechanism whose work and methods have caused serious questions, and to prejudge the outcome of any review. The authors rejected our amendments, including a reasonable six-month technical extension and the fundamental requirement that the Mechanism not attribute responsibility before the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission has completed its work and its conclusions have been properly considered by the Council.

We regret that the Council has again been pushed into division. But we cannot accept a text that politicizes the chemical weapons file, that fails to guarantee the independence, impartiality and evidentiary rigor of the Mechanism, and that seeks to turn the Security Council into an instrument for pressuring the Syrian Government and undermining the political process. The Joint Investigative Mechanism must not become a mechanism for predetermined conclusions. Its work must be based on credible, verifiable evidence and must respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic.

The Russian Federation remains ready for constructive, professional work to ensure accountability for chemical weapons use. We call for objective investigation of every serious incident, including those that have not been properly examined. But we will not support attempts to impose deadlines, to divide the Council, or to create a mechanism that serves political goals rather than the truth. We therefore voted against this draft, and we will continue to insist on an impartial and balanced approach.
after.Senegal: Mr. President, Senegal voted in favour of the draft resolution and deeply regrets that the Council has again been unable to preserve the mandate of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism. We supported this technical extension because the use of chemical weapons can never be justified, and because the Mechanism must be able to continue its impartial, independent and objective work. The failure to renew its mandate creates a dangerous vacuum in accountability and weakens the international norm against chemical weapons. Senegal calls on all parties in Syria, including the Syrian Government, to cooperate fully and without preconditions with the OPCW and the Mechanism and to ensure safe and unhindered access. We urge the Council to overcome its divisions and return to the spirit of consensus that produced resolutions 2118 (2013) and 2235 (2015), so that accountability can be upheld. This effort must also be accompanied by a political solution based on the Geneva communiqué and resolution 2254 (2015).
after.Sweden:
Mr President,

Sweden voted in favour of this draft resolution and co-sponsored it. We deeply regret that the Security Council has once again been unable to unite behind the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism. The JIM’s mandate expires tomorrow. A 30-day technical extension was a modest, reasonable and necessary step: it would have preserved the Mechanism’s ability to continue its impartial work while the Council considered its mandate and working methods. It did not prejudge that review, and it should not have been a controversial proposition.

The use of chemical weapons is a serious violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. There can be no impunity for those responsible. The JIM’s objective, independent investigations are essential to upholding the global norm against chemical weapons and to preserving the credibility of this Council. We regret that the draft was not adopted owing to the negative vote of a permanent member.

This is a setback, but it is not the end. Sweden will not stop working for accountability and for a united Council position. We urge all members to return to the table in good faith, and we call on all parties in Syria, including the Syrian Government, to cooperate fully and without preconditions with the OPCW and the JIM. The Council must not allow the Mechanism’s expertise and evidence to be lost, and it must not signal that chemical weapons can be used without consequence.

Thank you.
after.Ukraine:
Mr. President,

Ukraine voted in favour of the draft resolution we have just considered and co-sponsored it because the OPCW–UN Joint Investigative Mechanism must not be allowed to lapse in the face of grave and continuing reports of chemical weapons use in Syria. We deeply regret that this Council has once again failed to act. A clear majority supported a technical extension, but the Russian Federation has used its veto to block accountability. This is not a technical defeat; it is a blow to the credibility of the Council and to the international norm against chemical weapons.

The mandate of the Joint Investigative Mechanism expires tomorrow. We cannot accept that the perpetrators of chemical weapons attacks, and those who shield them, are allowed to escape scrutiny. The Russian Federation’s veto does not erase the evidence, nor does it create impunity in law. Ukraine will continue to support the independent, impartial and objective work of the Joint Investigative Mechanism and the OPCW, and we call on all parties in Syria, including the Syrian Government, to cooperate fully and without preconditions. We also call on Council members not to use the forthcoming review as a pretext to weaken or dismantle the Mechanism.

Ukraine remains committed to accountability. The Council’s failure today only strengthens our resolve.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr President, the United Kingdom is deeply disappointed that the Russian Federation has once again used its veto to prevent this Council from upholding accountability for the use of chemical weapons in Syria. This draft resolution was a limited, technical extension of the Joint Investigative Mechanism for 30 days. It did not prejudge the Mechanism’s findings, and it did not pre-empt the comprehensive review. It simply sought to preserve the JIM’s capacity and avoid an operational gap at a time when its work is more necessary than ever.

The result is clear: 12 members voted in favour, and only two against. The majority of this Council supported keeping the JIM alive. Russia’s veto will not protect anyone from the truth. It will not erase the findings of the JIM’s report. It will only make it harder to identify and hold accountable those who have used chemical weapons in Syria, including the Syrian regime. The JIM’s mandate expires tomorrow, and we regret that the Council has been prevented from extending it.

The United Kingdom will continue to support the OPCW, the JIM’s independent and impartial work, and all efforts to ensure accountability. We call on Russia to reconsider its position, and we call on all parties in Syria to cooperate fully and without preconditions with the OPCW and any future accountability mechanism. Chemical weapons use must never be allowed to go unpunished.
after.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States is deeply disappointed that the Council has failed to extend the mandate of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism, even for a technical period of 30 days. We voted in favour of this resolution because the JIM’s impartial, expert work is essential to accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria. The Russian Federation’s veto does not change the facts. The use of chemical weapons is a grave violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. The JIM has documented repeated chemical weapons attacks, and its report of 26 October underscores the need for continued investigation. Those responsible must be held accountable; the victims of these attacks deserve no less. We reject any suggestion that the work of the JIM is politicized when it is the evidence and the conclusions that are inconvenient for some. We regret that the Council has been prevented from preserving an essential mechanism, and we will continue to work with all partners who are committed to upholding the chemical weapons taboo and to ensuring accountability. The United States will not allow this issue to be buried. We remain determined to pursue accountability through all appropriate means. Thank you.
